variants.redirect: If no ambiguity remains, add evidence or an inference instead.

attempts.name: Invite objections
attempts.adverse: Objections become a performance with no consequential revision.
attempts.old_benefit: Discover a constraint or counterexample the current account misses.
attempts.intended_effect: An objection exposes a material defect or increases warranted confidence within a stated scope.

variants.name: Find the controlling objection
variants.use_when: A proposal has many possible criticisms of unequal importance.
steps: Identify the assumption whose failure would invalidate the proposal
construct its strongest relevant objection
inspect available evidence
repair or reject the proposal if necessary.
variants.redirect: If the objection is already resolved, move to another consequential assumption.

variants.name: Construct a countermodel
variants.use_when: A claimed inference may fail despite its premises holding.
steps: Write the premises precisely
construct a case satisfying them
test whether the conclusion can still fail
narrow or repair the inference when it does.
variants.redirect: If no countermodel is found, do not mistake unsuccessful search for proof.

variants.name: Stress the execution path
variants.use_when: The idea may be sound but its implementation fragile.
steps: Trace the required sequence
insert a plausible missing input or disturbance
identify where execution fails
add a feasible branch for that condition.
variants.redirect: If recovery is infeasible, state the operating limit rather than hiding it.

attempts.name: State common ground
attempts.adverse: An appearance of consensus hides the actual disagreement.
attempts.old_benefit: Localize the remaining difference so effort can address it.
attempts.intended_effect: Shared premises enable a new inference, coordinated action, or precise disagreement.

variants.name: Derive from accepted facts
variants.use_when: Relevant facts are shared but their consequence is unused.
steps: Select the agreed facts
connect them through an explicit valid inference
state the new consequence
apply it to the current issue.
variants.redirect: If the consequence is already accepted, address the remaining disagreement.

variants.name: Coordinate compatible values
variants.use_when: Different priorities can support one action for different reasons.
steps: State each endorsed priority
find an action advancing both under actual constraints
inspect remaining trade-offs
propose the action without claiming identical values.
variants.redirect: If compatibility fails, present the real conflict.

variants.name: Align definitions
variants.use_when: Apparent disagreement may arise from different uses of a term.
steps: Specify each usage
translate the disputed claim into observable statements
compare those statements
retain any substantive disagreement after translation.
variants.redirect: If definitions were already shared, do not prolong semantic work.

attempts.name: Offer format choices
attempts.adverse: Choosing how to receive help becomes another burdensome task.
attempts.old_benefit: Let the person use a representation that materially reduces their difficulty.
attempts.intended_effect: The representation reduces the operation needed to understand or use the information.

variants.name: Choose a table or spatial mapping
variants.use_when: The task requires comparing exact relationships.
steps: Identify the comparison operation
assign consistent rows, columns, or positions
place comparable quantities on the same basis
expose the difference that controls the conclusion.
variants.redirect: If spatial form adds decoding effort, use direct prose.

variants.name: Choose interaction for changing conditions
variants.use_when: Understanding depends on how an outcome changes with inputs.
steps: Identify the consequential inputs
bind them to an explicit model
let changes reveal the resulting differences
state assumptions and unsupported regions.
variants.redirect: If a single static case answers the question, avoid building unnecessary interaction.

variants.name: Choose a direct sequence
variants.use_when: The user needs to execute dependent actions.
steps: Identify the required output
list actions in dependency order
attach conditions at the relevant steps
end at the completed output.
variants.redirect: If a format preference is already known, honor it unless it prevents the required operation.

attempts.name: Sequence several messages
attempts.adverse: The crucial point arrives only after attention or patience is exhausted.
attempts.old_benefit: Order the necessary changes so each prepares the next.
attempts.intended_effect: The message sequence supplies prerequisites and advances toward a result without redundant turns.

variants.name: Order by understanding dependencies
variants.use_when: A later inference requires an earlier concept.
steps: Identify the desired inference
trace its prerequisites
supply only missing prerequisites first
derive and apply the inference as soon as they are available.
variants.redirect: If prerequisites are already known, begin with the inference.

variants.name: Lead with the consequential contrast
variants.use_when: A familiar explanation would be ignored before its novelty appears.
steps: Identify the difference that changes the decision
present it first
provide the evidence needed to establish it
add context only where it changes interpretation.
variants.redirect: If the contrast overstates the evidence, narrow it before using it.

variants.name: Make every turn advance
variants.use_when: A continuing conversation risks cycling through acknowledgments.
steps: Track the last established result
identify the next unresolved dependency
resolve it in the next message
update the shared result rather than repeating the trajectory.
variants.redirect: If no dependency remains, complete the task and stop.

attempts.name: Supply an immediate answer
attempts.adverse: A premature answer anchors interpretation before the question is understood.
attempts.old_benefit: Provide the exact missing fact that enables the next inference.
attempts.intended_effect: The immediate answer resolves the actual question at the warranted scope.

variants.name: Supply a settled fact
variants.use_when: The question has a verifiable bounded answer.
steps: Identify the exact fact requested
verify it when needed
state it directly
include only qualifications that change its use.
variants.redirect: If the fact is unavailable, state the gap and obtain it where feasible.

variants.name: Give the supported verdict
variants.use_when: Existing information is enough to choose or assess.
steps: Apply the stated criterion
compare the live alternatives
give the conclusion first
explain the decisive reason and material limitation.
variants.redirect: If the criterion is missing but consequential, resolve it before claiming a best choice.

variants.name: Answer conditionally
variants.use_when: Several unresolved conditions imply different answers.
steps: Identify the smallest consequential branching condition
give the answer under each plausible branch
state which branch current evidence supports
obtain missing information only if needed to act.
variants.redirect: If one action works across branches, recommend that action directly.

attempts.name: Use humor
attempts.adverse: The attempt trivializes a consequential concern.
attempts.old_benefit: Create a memorable distinction or release tension that obstructs examination.
attempts.intended_effect: Humor supports a correct distinction, easier engagement, or accurate recall.

variants.name: Expose an incongruity
variants.use_when: A harmless contradiction can make a logical error visible.
steps: Identify the exact inconsistency
construct a brief analogous absurdity
connect the humor back to the actual inference
supply the corrected reasoning.
variants.redirect: If the joke changes the issue or humiliates the recipient, omit it.

variants.name: Release conversational tension
variants.use_when: Tension interferes with a task and the context permits humor.
steps: Choose a low-stakes feature of the situation
use brief nonpersonal humor
return immediately to the substantive issue
judge usefulness by continued engagement, not laughter alone.
variants.redirect: If the topic or response indicates distress, use direct considerate language.

variants.name: Attach an accurate mnemonic
variants.use_when: A rule needs a memorable retrieval cue.
steps: Identify the rule's essential relation
build a short humorous image around it
keep the exception visible
use the cue to retrieve and apply the rule.
variants.redirect: If the joke outlives the accurate rule, replace it.

attempts.name: Tell a story
attempts.adverse: Narrative coherence substitutes for causal or evidential support.
attempts.old_benefit: Make a process understandable without hiding where the example is limited.
attempts.intended_effect: The story conveys a warranted causal or decision structure that can be used beyond the story.

variants.name: Trace a mechanism through events
variants.use_when: An abstract process is hard to follow.
steps: Choose a representative documented or clearly fictional case
show each consequential event
connect actions to outcomes without unsupported causation
extract the governing relation.
variants.redirect: If the case is exceptional, label what it can and cannot establish.

variants.name: Make a decision visible
variants.use_when: The audience needs to understand a choice under constraints.
steps: Show what the actor knew at the time
present the feasible alternatives
explain the trade-off that governed the choice
compare the result with the quality of the decision process.
variants.redirect: If the story relies on hindsight, revise it to preserve the actual uncertainty.

variants.name: Transfer the story's structure
variants.use_when: A memorable case risks remaining an isolated anecdote.
steps: Identify its functional roles
compare them with a second case
name the shared relation and differing conditions
apply only the transferable relation to the present problem.
variants.redirect: If the mapping fails, keep the story as illustration rather than evidence.

attempts.name: End with a next step
attempts.adverse: Generic invitations keep the interaction going without improving it.
attempts.old_benefit: Identify the next operation that would resolve a live issue.
attempts.intended_effect: The ending completes the work or specifies an action that advances an unresolved dependency.

variants.name: Implement the supported decision
variants.use_when: The choice is settled and execution is authorized.
steps: Identify the first remaining operation
supply its inputs
carry out the authorized work
report the concrete result and any material limit.
variants.redirect: If execution is blocked, identify the actual blocker rather than offering generic encouragement.

variants.name: Resolve the missing input
variants.use_when: One unavailable fact or resource blocks completion.
steps: Name that input precisely
identify who or what can supply it
obtain it within authorization where possible
state the conditional action that follows.
variants.redirect: If the user alone can supply it, ask one concise question.

variants.name: Stop at completion
variants.use_when: The requested result is already delivered.
steps: Compare the result with the request
confirm material requirements are met
present the result accessibly
end without manufacturing another task.
variants.redirect: If a real requirement remains, complete it or state the precise limitation.

attempts.name: Optimize approval
attempts.adverse: Agreement and flattery are rewarded despite worse understanding.
attempts.old_benefit: Use experience feedback alongside evidence of accuracy, agency, and capability.
attempts.intended_effect: Approval informs delivery preferences without replacing accuracy or the person's endorsed aims.

variants.name: Separate liking from correctness
variants.use_when: Positive reaction may conceal factual or practical defects.
steps: Record what was liked
inspect the substantive claim independently
retain accurate useful elements
repair errors even if they were well received.
variants.redirect: If approval is the actual legitimate outcome, still identify any material deception or cost.

variants.name: Optimize for endorsed aims
variants.use_when: Immediate gratification conflicts with a stated longer-term goal.
steps: Identify the goal already endorsed
compare responses by their effect on that goal
choose the useful response
make the immediate trade-off explicit where relevant.
variants.redirect: If the longer-term goal is assumed, do not impose it.

variants.name: Use honest disagreement
variants.use_when: The requested conclusion is not supported.
steps: State the supported conclusion plainly
identify the decisive evidence or inference
preserve the valid part of the user's concern
provide a constructive consequence.
variants.redirect: If the evidence changes, update rather than defending disagreement for its own sake.

attempts.name: Optimize novelty
attempts.adverse: Unfamiliarity is pursued even when the new idea is irrelevant or false.
attempts.old_benefit: Find a consequential distinction the person does not already have available.
attempts.intended_effect: Novelty adds a useful capability, warranted inference, or available option.

variants.name: Derive a new consequence
variants.use_when: The ingredients are familiar but their implication is unused.
steps: Select accepted premises
combine them in a valid relevant way
derive the previously unused consequence
show what the person can now decide or do differently.
variants.redirect: If the consequence is already known, move to a remaining dependency.

variants.name: Supply a new operation
variants.use_when: Existing knowledge cannot currently be put to use.
steps: Identify the missing transformation
teach or perform that operation
connect it to the existing knowledge
produce the useful output.
variants.redirect: If the operation changes no relevant capability, omit it.

variants.name: Remove an unnecessary problem
variants.use_when: Effort is aimed at a task built on a false necessity.
steps: Identify the assumed requirement
check whether the valued outcome depends on it
show a route that avoids it
retire the unnecessary work where justified.
variants.redirect: If the requirement is real, do not call dismissal an insight.

attempts.name: Optimize speed
attempts.adverse: Premature closure creates a fast but wrong interpretation.
attempts.old_benefit: Use the shortest route that preserves what the person needs to infer and act.
attempts.intended_effect: Total effort to a sufficiently good result decreases without losing a material requirement.

variants.name: Prune unnecessary dependencies
variants.use_when: The workflow contains steps unrelated to the required result.
steps: Define the sufficient result
trace which steps actually support it
remove redundant or irrelevant steps
complete the remaining dependency chain.
variants.redirect: If removing a step changes validity or usability, restore its necessary function.

variants.name: Use an easier representation
variants.use_when: Much effort comes from transforming the information mentally.
steps: Identify the difficult operation
encode the same information in a form that performs part of it externally
preserve denominators, relations, and limits
complete the remaining comparison.
variants.redirect: If the representation loses information that changes the answer, revise it.

variants.name: Choose the cheapest decisive operation
variants.use_when: Several investigations could resolve the issue.
steps: Identify which outcomes would change the conclusion
compare available operations by cost and discrimination
perform the cheapest adequate one
stop once the consequential uncertainty is resolved.
variants.redirect: If no operation is decisive, report the supported partial result rather than overclaiming speed.

attempts.name: Measure agreement
attempts.adverse: Social compliance is recorded as genuine understanding.
attempts.old_benefit: Assess the actual belief, skill, decision, or capability that matters.
attempts.intended_effect: Agreement is interpreted at its actual scope and supplemented only by observations needed for the goal.

variants.name: Observe transfer
variants.use_when: The claimed change concerns understanding a rule.
steps: Identify the agreed rule
present or observe a fresh relevant case
inspect rule selection and application
infer understanding only to that demonstrated scope.
variants.redirect: If observation is unavailable, record expressed agreement without claiming transfer.

variants.name: Observe a decision consequence
variants.use_when: The claim should alter a real choice.
steps: Specify the choice affected
identify how the accepted claim should change it
observe the person's actual reasoning or action where available
distinguish constraints from failure to update.
variants.redirect: If the claim changes no decision, assess the relevant nondecision target instead.

variants.name: Separate assent from confidence
variants.use_when: Politeness or ambiguity may make agreement hard to interpret.
steps: Clarify the exact proposition only if needed
allow disagreement without penalty
obtain an unleading confidence judgment when useful
preserve unresolved uncertainty in the record.
variants.redirect: If measurement would burden a simple exchange, leave the effect unverified.

attempts.name: Reuse a previously successful method
attempts.adverse: Success in one starting state is treated as evidence for every later state.
attempts.old_benefit: Reuse the method when the conditions that explain its usefulness are present.
attempts.intended_effect: A previously useful method is reused only where its causal prerequisites still apply.

variants.name: Match the causal conditions
variants.use_when: A past success suggests a reusable intervention.
steps: Identify what changed previously
reconstruct the likely enabling conditions
compare them with the present case
reuse the relevant operations where those conditions hold.
variants.redirect: If the original cause is unknown, treat reuse as provisional rather than established.

variants.name: Detect changed circumstances
variants.use_when: A once-effective routine is losing value.
steps: Identify the original validity conditions
inspect changes in task, resources, or recipient state
locate the condition that no longer holds
revise or replace the affected branch.
variants.redirect: If conditions are stable, inspect execution or measurement before redesigning.

variants.name: Recombine components
variants.use_when: Only part of a previous method fits.
steps: Separate its operations by function
retain the operations matching current needs
replace incompatible operations
inspect the combined sequence for missing dependencies.
variants.redirect: If interactions make the combination invalid, use a coherent alternative.

attempts.name: Personalize from feedback
attempts.adverse: A mistaken model of the person becomes more entrenched.
attempts.old_benefit: Update the model from specific evidence, including evidence that contradicts it.
attempts.intended_effect: Feedback improves the user model without turning one response into a permanent personality claim.

variants.name: Update a demonstrated preference
variants.use_when: Feedback identifies a specific useful or harmful feature.
steps: Extract the feature named
connect it to the task condition
change the relevant response behavior
observe subsequent task results without demanding praise.
variants.redirect: If the feedback is broad, use the narrowest interpretation supported by context.

variants.name: Retain competing explanations
variants.use_when: One reaction supports several possible diagnoses.
steps: List the consequential explanations
compare each with visible evidence
choose a response useful across the plausible explanations
ask only if their difference blocks progress.
variants.redirect: If the response fails again, update the diagnosis rather than intensifying the same tactic.

variants.name: Retire a stale assumption
variants.use_when: Past personalization conflicts with current instructions or evidence.
steps: Identify the conflicting assumption
give current explicit instructions priority
remove the obsolete constraint
adapt the present work accordingly.
variants.redirect: If the conflict is unresolved, keep the adaptation conditional.

attempts.name: Summarize for later reuse
attempts.adverse: Compression strips out the boundary that made the claim correct.
attempts.old_benefit: Preserve the decisive relationship, conditions, and remaining uncertainty.
attempts.intended_effect: The summary preserves what a future user needs to infer or act correctly.

variants.name: Preserve decision structure
variants.use_when: A later reader must reuse a conclusion.
steps: State the conclusion
include its controlling reasons
preserve conditions that would reverse it
provide the action implied under those conditions.
variants.redirect: If compression removes a reversal condition, expand the summary.

variants.name: Preserve scope and uncertainty
variants.use_when: A qualified result may become an overgeneralized slogan.
steps: Identify its population, task, and boundary
attach the material uncertainty to the claim
include a representative use condition
link supporting detail where useful.
variants.redirect: If the short form misleads when quoted alone, rewrite the short form.

variants.name: Separate core from recoverable detail
variants.use_when: The original material is too large for frequent reuse.
steps: Identify the recurring use task
keep information needed for that task in the core
place supporting detail behind explicit references
verify that the core still supports the intended operation.
variants.redirect: If different tasks need different cores, create purpose-specific summaries.

attempts.name: Evaluate each sentence in isolation
attempts.adverse: Prerequisites are removed because their contribution occurs through later material.
attempts.old_benefit: Assess the necessary sequence together with its total cost and consequences.
attempts.intended_effect: Evaluation captures how statements jointly produce a useful result.

variants.name: Evaluate a dependency block
variants.use_when: Individual sentences supply prerequisites for one inference.
steps: Identify the conclusion the block produces
map each sentence's contribution
remove only sentences whose function is redundant
judge the resulting inference as a whole.
variants.redirect: If a sentence has no useful function, delete it.

variants.name: Inspect the combined effect
variants.use_when: Individually accurate statements may jointly imply something false.
steps: Read the sequence as a recipient would
identify its likely implication
compare that implication with the evidence
revise order or qualifications to correct it.
variants.redirect: If the implication is uncertain, make the intended relationship explicit.

variants.name: Evaluate the complete representation
variants.use_when: Meaning depends on tables, examples, or visual relationships.
steps: Identify the operation the whole representation supports
inspect labels and relations together
check the conclusion a reader can derive
repair any missing or misleading connection.
variants.redirect: If the representation cannot support the operation, change its form.

attempts.name: Repeat human–AI feedback
attempts.adverse: Small errors are amplified and then reintroduced as apparently independent support.
attempts.old_benefit: Keep reliable external checks and independent evidence available to interrupt error accumulation.
attempts.intended_effect: Iteration improves externally anchored accuracy or usefulness without laundering repeated model output into evidence.

variants.name: Anchor revisions externally
variants.use_when: AI and user judgments repeatedly influence one another.
steps: Identify the claim or output being revised
choose an independent observation or specification
compare each revision with that anchor
retain changes supported by the comparison.
variants.redirect: If no independent anchor exists, mark the result as a hypothesis.

variants.name: Trace genuinely new information
variants.use_when: Repeated agreement is increasing confidence.
steps: List the evidence added on each round
trace its origins
merge repetitions of the same source
update confidence only for new relevant information or valid inference.
variants.redirect: If nothing new was added, do not count another round as corroboration.

variants.name: Preserve a recoverable revision history
variants.use_when: Iterations may drift away from the original objective.
steps: Record the accepted objective and prior supported result
identify each material revision and its reason
inspect downstream consequences
restore the prior result if the revision fails its criterion.
variants.redirect: If the objective itself changes, record that change separately from factual improvement.

attempts.name: Ask whether learning felt effective
attempts.adverse: Fluency and ease are mistaken for durable learning.
attempts.old_benefit: Distinguish the experience of learning from what can later be recalled or used.
attempts.intended_effect: Subjective learning experience is distinguished from the capability the activity was meant to produce.

variants.name: Separate experience from performance
variants.use_when: An activity feels easy, difficult, or satisfying.
steps: Record the experience as experience
specify the intended capability
inspect a relevant performance when available
judge usability and learning on their separate evidence.
variants.redirect: If performance is unobserved, do not infer it from the feeling.

variants.name: Compare predicted and retained knowledge
variants.use_when: Immediate fluency may mislead judgments of future recall.
steps: Estimate what will remain available after a meaningful delay
revisit without the answer in view
compare recall with the estimate
revise the preferred study method accordingly.
variants.redirect: If the task only requires immediate assisted use, evaluate that actual goal instead.

variants.name: Check unfamiliar application
variants.use_when: The intended gain is transferable understanding.
steps: Choose a new case requiring the same principle
remove irrelevant hints from the original example
perform the relevant operation
compare the result with the intended standard.
variants.redirect: If only familiar cases succeed, target the missing recognition or adaptation skill.

sources.title: Roediger & Karpicke (2006)
sources.scope: In two experiments with prose passages, repeated study outperformed prior testing at five minutes, but prior testing produced greater retention at two days or one week. Restudying also increased confidence. Supports a divergence between immediate performance, confidence, and delayed recall in these learning tasks; does not establish that difficulty always helps.

sources.title: Deslauriers et al. (2019)
sources.scope: Randomly assigned college physics students learned more with active instruction while reporting a lower feeling of learning than students receiving passive instruction with the same content. A result about these instructional conditions; self-reported benefit remains useful evidence about experience and cannot alone establish learning.

sources.title: Schultz et al. (2007)
sources.scope: Household energy feedback about average neighborhood consumption produced savings among higher consumers and an undesirable increase among lower consumers. Adding a message of social approval or disapproval eliminated the boomerang effect in the experiment. Direct evidence that the sign of a norm message can depend on the recipient's starting behavior; the result does not make all normative messages beneficial.

sources.title: Wood & Porter (2019)
sources.scope: Across five experiments involving more than 10,100 participants and 52 issues, the researchers found no factual corrections that produced the tested backfire effect. Corrective information does not routinely strengthen the corrected false belief. This result does not rule out relational, motivational, or other adverse consequences.

sources.title: Eskreis-Winkler et al. (2019)
sources.scope: In a preregistered randomized field experiment involving 1,982 high school students, giving motivational advice to younger students improved advisers' grades in math and a self-selected target class across an academic quarter. Supports an effect of the advice-giving intervention in this setting. The abstract does not establish one uniquely responsible psychological mechanism or a large universal effect.

sources.title: Glickman & Sharot (2025)
sources.scope: Across experiments with 1,401 participants, human–AI feedback loops amplified human biases in perceptual, emotional, and social judgments. Participants often underestimated the influence. Supports harmful feedback effects in the studied tasks. It does not establish that every chatbot interaction has these effects or that beneficial amplification is symmetrical.

sources.title: Fernbach et al. (2013)
sources.scope: Generating detailed mechanistic policy explanations reduced an illusion of understanding and moderated attitudes in the experiments; enumerating reasons for preferences did not have the same effect. Supports a difference between two elicited operations in these tasks. Moderation is not itself a general measure of truth, and this is not a universal prescription to moderate beliefs.

sources.title: Yeager et al. (2019)
sources.scope: A brief growth-mindset intervention improved grades among lower-achieving students and increased overall advanced-mathematics enrollment in a nationally representative US high-school sample; effects varied with context. Supports context-sensitive motivational intervention effects, not guaranteed or uniformly large benefits from generic encouragement.

sources.title: Hulleman & Harackiewicz (2009)
sources.scope: A randomized field experiment asked students to connect science coursework with their lives. Interest and course grades increased for students with low expectations of success. Supports learner-generated relevance in the specified subgroup and context. It does not imply that imposing a supposedly relevant motive will work.

sources.title: Fazio et al. (2015)
sources.scope: The experiments investigated repetition-based increases in perceived truth, including cases where participants had relevant knowledge. Supports concern about familiarity being used as evidence of truth. It does not establish that repeating a false claim within a clear correction routinely backfires.

sources.title: Mellers et al. (2014)
sources.scope: In a geopolitical forecasting tournament, probability training, team collaboration, and tracking top performers were associated with improved calibration and resolution. Training included reference classes and combining estimates. Tracking selected high performers, so it must not be interpreted as a purely randomized training effect. Supports concrete forecasting ingredients in this setting, not guaranteed individual calibration.

sources.title: Gentner, Loewenstein & Thompson (2003)
sources.scope: Three studies of novice negotiation learning found benefits from comparing cases for extracting and transferring common structure; support for comparison improved transfer. Supports explicit relational comparison in those tasks. It does not establish that every analogy, example pair, or newly assembled transfer sequence works.

sources.title: Kornell & Bjork (2008)
sources.scope: Participants learned artists' styles from paintings presented in blocks or interleaved with other artists. Interleaving improved classification of new paintings, although participants judged blocked presentation more effective. Supports discrimination and subjective-performance divergence in this category-learning task. It is not evidence that all kinds of contextual variation or difficulty improve every skill.

sources.title: van der Bles et al. (2020)
sources.scope: Experiments on communicating uncertainty about facts and numbers found increased perceived uncertainty with only small decreases in trust, mostly for verbal uncertainty communication. Supports specifying uncertainty without assuming catastrophic loss of trust. It does not promise preserved trust for every formulation, source, audience, or topic.

sources.title: Carrera et al. (2018)
sources.scope: In a randomized study with 877 gym members, selecting intended attendance days and times did not increase attendance relative to recording prior exercise. The authors reported a tightly estimated null despite participant engagement with planning. Direct evidence that performing a plausible planning procedure can fail to change repeated behavior; the catalog's proposed diagnostic branches require their own validation.

sources.title: Lally et al. (2010)
sources.scope: Volunteers chose a behavior to repeat daily in the same context over 12 weeks and reported behavior and automaticity. The study modeled habit development from these longitudinal observations. It supports investigating context, repetition, and changing automaticity, but does not supply a universal completion date or randomized proof of the catalog's habit-building recipes.

sources.title: Gross (1998)
sources.scope: In a laboratory study using a disgusting film, reappraisal and expressive suppression both reduced expressive behavior, but differed in reported disgust and physiological response. Supports distinguishing appraisal, feeling, expression, and physiology. It does not establish that reframing improves every emotion, that suppression is always harmful, or that ordinary conversational recipes treat clinical problems.

sources.title: Walton et al. (2023)
sources.scope: A randomized study with 26,911 students at 22 institutions evaluated a brief social-belonging intervention. Benefits for first-year full-time progress depended on student group and college context; effects occurred where groups had opportunities to belong. Supports treating actual opportunity as a consequential condition, not assuming a message can compensate for every exclusionary environment.

sources.title: Hoffrage et al. (2000)
sources.scope: Natural-frequency representations improved reasoning about statistical information in the studied tasks. The relevant representation preserves joint counts and the appropriate denominator; merely replacing every percentage with an isolated count is not the same operation. Supports the representational ingredient of the probability example, not a universal advantage for every table or numerical format.

sources.title: Renkl, Atkinson & Große (2004)
sources.scope: Two experiments investigated fading worked solution steps in a computer-based learning environment. Fading supported learning, with fewer unproductive learning events; the proposed increase in productive self-explanation events was not found. Supports a specified instructional ingredient while illustrating why a plausible mediator must not be presented as established.

sources.title: Bastani et al. (2025)
sources.scope: A high-school mathematics field experiment compared ordinary GPT assistance with a tutor design containing safeguards. Unguarded assistance improved practice performance but harmed later unassisted performance; the tutor design largely mitigated that harm. Supports separating assisted output from independent learning and attending to tool design. It does not show that all AI assistance harms learning or that this catalog's scaffolds are validated. An author-hosted version is available at https://hamsabastani.github.io/education_llm.pdf.

sources.title: Milkman et al. (2021)
sources.scope: A megastudy tested 54 four-week digital programs among 61,293 fitness-chain members; effects differed across programs, with 45% significantly increasing weekly visits during the intervention. This motivates comparative evaluation of complete procedures in a common setting. Statistical significance is not a per-person success probability, and a selected top performer is not automatically best in a new setting.

sources.title: Milkman et al. (2011)
sources.scope: A field experiment on a one-time vaccination opportunity found a 4.2 percentage-point increase from prompting people to write both a date and a time. A date-only prompt had a smaller, nonsignificant difference. Supports a specific planning intervention with an available opportunity; it neither guarantees action nor transfers automatically to recurring behavior.
